newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle slowing into holiday-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle slowing into holiday-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Wednesday were slowing going into the Independence Day holiday on Friday, feedlot sources said.
Major U.S. cattle slaughter and processing plants will be closed for the holiday, with a few expected open on Saturday, company officials said.

Tuesday's active sales, coupled with large numbers of formulated or contract cattle, provided packers with enough cattle to restart plants following the Independence Day holiday on Friday, feedlot sources said.
Packers Wednesday lowered bids $1.00 at $62.00, with owners pricing remaining cattle at $63.00, unchanged from Tuesday's sale.
Sales in Kansas were too light to test and there were no reported trades in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, the feedlot sources said.

Outlooks for continued sales at $63.00 were slipping amid lower beef prices on Wednesday and perceptions that beef demand seasonally dips following the long holiday weekend, several cattle sources said. Projections for increased cattle supplies this summer also could weigh on prices, they said.
